extracted.intended_audience: state air quality agencies and SIP submitters (state environmental agencies, EPA regional staffs, environmental attorneys and stakeholders)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and procedural requirements for EPA approval of a State Implementation Plan (SIP) certification that a State's emission statement program satisfies Clean Air Act requirements for specified ozone NAAQS classifications. Covers substantive legal standards, regulatory cross‑references, and procedural/publication requirements for SIP approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: CAA compliance requirement for SIP approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the CAA, the Administrator is required to approve a SIP submission that complies with the provisions of the CAA and applicable Federal regulations. 42 U.S.C. 7410(k); 40 CFR 52.02(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA's role is to approve state choices, provided that they meet the criteria of the CAA. Thus, in reviewing SIP submissions, the EPA approves state law only if it complies with statutory and regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emission Statement Program certification (by NAAQS/classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: State must certify that it has satisfied the requirements for an emission statement program pursuant to the Clean Air Act sections applicable to the area's classification (e.g., CAA section 182(a)(3)(B) and 182(b) for 2015 Moderate; CAA section 182(a)(3)(B) and 182(c) for 2008 Serious).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification should identify the NAAQS and classification (e.g., 2008 8‑hour Ozone NAAQS—Serious; 2015 8‑hour Ozone NAAQS—Moderate) and the applicable nonattainment area(s). Example: New York submitted certifications for the NY‑NJ‑CT nonattainment area on 1/29/2021 and 11/29/2021.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate enforceable implementation through a federally approved state regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: The emission statement requirement must be fully addressed through implementation and enforcement of a state‑wide federally approved regulation (e.g., 6 NYCRR subpart 202‑2, 'Emission Statements').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SIP submittal should show that the state's regulation is in effect and being enforced; EPA may rely on prior federal approval of the regulation (e.g., EPA approval of 6 NYCRR subpart 202‑2 into the SIP on 12/28/2023) as evidence that requirements are addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with applicable CFR provisions (40 CFR 51.1115 and 40 CFR 51.1315)
rubrics_metrics.description: The State's emission statement regulation and certification must be consistent with relevant Federal regulations governing emission statements (e.g., 40 CFR 51.1115 and 40 CFR 51.1315).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA will determine whether the state's regulation 'continues to properly implement the emissions statement requirements' consistent with these CFR sections when approving the certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment period on proposed rule (30 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA provides a public review and comment period for proposed SIP approval actions (example: 30‑day review and comment period for the May 8, 2025 proposed rule; comment period ended June 9, 2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive comments may prompt changes to the final rule; absence of comments may result in no changes to the final action. The proposed rule should clearly identify how to submit comments and the comment deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docketing and public availability of supporting materials via Regulations.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA establishes a docket for the action (e.g., Docket ID No. EPA‑R02‑OAR‑2025‑0040) and lists all documents in the docket on Regulations.gov; some materials may not be publicly available (CUI/CBI) while publicly available docket materials are available electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SIP submittals should include supporting documents and technical appendices; the docket should reference and, where appropriate, provide access to supporting TSDs, inventories, and other appendices (examples: multiple appendices and TSDs listed as supporting documents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and recordation in 40 CFR part 52 tables
rubrics_metrics.description: When EPA approves SIP elements, the action is reflected in §52.1670 (Identification of plan) and related tables in 40 CFR part 52, with entries that show the action/SIP element, applicable geographic or nonattainment area, New York submittal date, EPA approval date, and an explanation (e.g., 'Full approval').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SIP approvals should provide the precise wording to be entered into the CFR tables (action description, area, dates, and explanation) so that the federal code reflects the approval accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review and filing deadlines under CAA section 307(b)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions for judicial review of a final SIP action must be filed in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the appropriate circuit by the deadline specified under CAA section 307(b)(1) (example: petitions must be filed by October 14, 2025 for this action).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a petition for reconsideration by the Administrator does not affect the finality of the action for purposes of judicial review and does not extend the time to file a petition for judicial review; failing to file within the statutory period may foreclose later challenges in enforcement proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and Executive Order applicability determinations for SIP approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA determines and states whether a SIP approval action is subject to various statutory and Executive Order review requirements (examples in this document: not a significant regulatory action under EO 12866; not subject to EO 14192; does not impose information collection burdens under the Paperwork Reduction Act; certified under the Regulatory Flexibility Act; does not contain unfunded mandates; no federalism implications; not subject to EO 13045 or EO 13211; not subject to National Technology Transfer and Advancement Act requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because SIP approvals 'merely approve state law as meeting Federal requirements,' EPA typically explains applicability or exemptions from listed statutes/EOs in the preamble; SIP submittals may address whether the submission raises issues under these statutes/EOs to facilitate EPA's determinations.
